label: Fish, shellfish and fish-derived food and feed products
description: Laws and official materials about the catching, trade, import, export, production, processing, management, marketing and labelling of fish, shellfish and fish-derived products. This includes seafood products from wild-caught, freshwater, harvested, aquaculture and farmed sources; live shellfish intended for human consumption; processed fish products used as human food or animal feed; and fish by-products used in food, beverage or feed production.
synonyms: fish oil for food or feed
fish bladders isinglass food beverage processing
exclusions: Ornamental aquatic species and ornamental fish kept for aquariums.
Aquarium fish and aquarium trade materials where the fish are not for human food, animal feed, aquaculture production, or food or beverage processing.
Fish kept as pets or pet-fish movements, welfare or trade.
Fish used for scientific research, laboratory testing or research-establishment purposes only.
Recreational fishing, sport fishing, angling, rod licences, leisure fishing permits and similar non-commercial fishing activities.

Fish conservation, biodiversity, habitat protection, species protection or ecological restoration materials where the operative purpose is conservation rather than catching, production, trade, marketing, food/feed use or aquaculture management.

Fish-derived products intended for non-food, non-feed and non-beverage uses, including cosmetics, personal care products, medical products, wound dressings, cosmetic collagen, industrial collagen and other industrial applications.

General marine environment, water quality, river basin, harbour, vessel safety or navigation materials unless they directly regulate fish, shellfish, aquaculture, seafood products, fishery products, fish-derived food/feed products, or commercial catching and landing.

General animal by-product materials unless they specifically concern fish, shellfish, fishery products, fishmeal, fish flour, fish oil, fish bladders, isinglass, caviar or other fish-derived products within the included food/feed/beverage scope.
Poultry hatchery, hatching egg, poultry chick or farmyard poultry instruments unless they materially regulate fish, shellfish or aquaculture.
Seed, potato, plant, crop or agricultural traceability instruments unless they materially regulate fish or fish-derived food/feed products.

metadata.conversion_note: Refined after fish discovery run BR1: added fisheries-law anchors, demoted broad standalone synonyms to weak_terms, strengthened AI triage noise guidance; BR1 quota cleanup demoted bare quota/TAC terms and added fish-specific quota compounds.

likely_accept: UK, Great Britain, England, Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland, assimilated EU or retained EU instruments directly regulating commercial catching, landing, sale or marketing of fish or shellfish.
Instruments regulating import, export, trade, certification, traceability or border controls for fish, shellfish, seafood or fishery products.
Aquaculture, fish farms, farmed fish, aquaculture fish hatcheries, fish reared from roe, or wild-caught fish subsequently fattened in captivity.
Seafood hygiene, processing, labelling, marketing standards or official controls for fish or shellfish for human consumption.
Fish-derived food, feed or beverage-production materials such as fishmeal, fish flour, fish pellets for animal feed, caviar, fish oil for food/feed, fish bladders or isinglass.

Fisheries management instruments that materially regulate commercial catching, fish stocks, quotas or TACs, fishing opportunities or effort, landings, gear restrictions, fishing vessel licensing or monitoring, fisheries enforcement, or market supply or sale — including where conservation language is present but the operative mechanism regulates commercial fisheries.
needs_human_review: Mixed fisheries and conservation instruments where commercial catching, quotas, fishing effort, landings, vessel licensing or seafood supply controls need legal review to confirm materiality.
Revoked or historical fisheries, aquaculture or seafood-trade instruments that may be predecessors of the current regime.
Northern Ireland or EU-derived material where post-Brexit applicability may require legal review.
Aquatic animal health, shellfish harvesting-area or disease rules linked to trade or human consumption but not clearly the principal subject.
park_contextual: General customs-code, trade-statistics or sanctions instruments where fish or seafood appears only as one commodity among many.
General animal by-product, waste or environmental instruments with incidental fish references.
Marine environment, water quality or harbour instruments adjacent to fisheries but not regulating catching, landings, trade or seafood products.
likely_reject: Ornamental, aquarium or pet fish instruments.
Recreational fishing, sport fishing, angling or rod-licence instruments.

Conservation, biodiversity, habitat or species-protection instruments with no material commercial catching, quota, fishing effort, landing, vessel licensing, fish trade, aquaculture or seafood supply controls.
Fish-derived non-food, non-feed and non-beverage products such as cosmetics, personal care, medical products, wound dressings or industrial collagen.
Poultry hatchery, hatching egg, poultry chick or farmyard poultry instruments unless they materially regulate fish, shellfish or aquaculture.
Seed, potato, plant, crop or agricultural traceability instruments unless they materially regulate fish or fish-derived food/feed products.

General customs-code, trade-statistics or sanctions instruments where fish or seafood is only one commodity among many and the instrument does not specifically regulate fish, shellfish, fishery products, aquaculture or seafood controls.
General animal by-product instruments unless fish-derived food/feed/beverage products are materially covered.
triage_guidance.triage_rule: Weak terms are supporting signals only and must not make a candidate likely_accept on their own. Bare quota, quotas and TAC matches are weak supporting signals only and must not make a candidate likely_accept on their own. General tariff quota, customs quota, agricultural quota, wood quota, industrial quota, carbon quota or sanctions quota instruments should be rejected or parked unless they specifically regulate fish, fishery products, shellfish, aquaculture, seafood trade or fisheries management. Prefer anchored compounds such as fish quota, fisheries quota, fish stock quota, total allowable catch fish, TAC fish stocks, aquaculture fish hatchery, fish pellets for animal feed, fish bladders isinglass food beverage processing, seafood import export marketing labelling, or fishery products traceability catch certificate. Do not exclude fisheries-management sources merely because they contain conservation language if the operative mechanism regulates commercial catching, fish stocks, quotas/TACs, fishing opportunities, fishing effort, landings, gear, vessel licensing, enforcement or seafood supply. Treat pet, ornamental, aquarium, research-only, recreational/sport fishing and non-food fish-derived product sources as out of scope unless commercial fisheries or seafood controls are materially covered.

inclusion_tests: Does the source regulate commercial catching, landing, sale or marketing of fish or shellfish?
Does it regulate import, export, certification, traceability or border control of fish, shellfish, seafood or fishery products?
Does it regulate aquaculture, fish farms, farmed fish, aquaculture fish hatcheries, fish reared from roe, or wild-caught fish subsequently fattened in captivity?
Does it regulate processing, labelling, presentation, hygiene, marketing standards or production of fish or shellfish for human consumption?
Does it regulate fish-derived food, feed or beverage-production materials such as fishmeal, fish flour, fish pellets for animal feed, caviar, fish oil for food/feed, fish bladders or isinglass?
Does it regulate fisheries management mechanisms such as quotas, TACs, fishing opportunities, fishing effort, fish stocks, landing obligation, fishing vessel licensing or fisheries enforcement?
exclusion_tests: Is the source only about ornamental, aquarium or pet fish?
Is the source only about recreational fishing, sport fishing, angling or leisure permits?
Is the source only about scientific research use of fish?

Is the source only about conservation, biodiversity, species protection or habitat restoration without material commercial catching, quota, fishing effort, landing, trade, aquaculture or seafood controls?
Is the source only about non-food fish-derived products such as cosmetics, personal care products, medical products, wound dressings or industrial collagen?
Is the source a poultry hatchery, seed/potato/plant traceability, general customs-code, trade-statistics or sanctions instrument where fish or seafood is incidental?
borderline_guidance: IUU fishing and catch-certificate rules are in scope where they regulate commercial fish imports, exports, landings, traceability or trade.
Shellfish disease, live bivalve mollusc and harvesting-area rules are in scope where linked to human consumption, trade, production, harvesting, processing or marketing.

Aquatic animal health rules are in scope where they materially regulate aquaculture, farmed fish, live shellfish for consumption, seafood movements or fish production; they are out of scope where they concern only pets, ornamental species, research animals or conservation.
Animal by-product rules are in scope only where fish-derived food/feed/beverage products or named fish by-products are materially covered.

Fisheries-management and mixed conservation/fisheries sources are in scope when they govern commercial catching, fish stocks, quotas/TACs, fishing opportunities, fishing effort, landings, gear restrictions, vessel licensing or monitoring, fisheries enforcement, or market supply or sale; they are out of scope only when conservation is the sole operative purpose with no material commercial fisheries mechanism.

Fish hatchery, roe, fish eggs, fish pellets, fish bladders, sturgeon products, seafood trade/marketing and fish traceability concepts are in scope only in aquaculture, fishery-product, food/feed/beverage or seafood trade contexts — not as standalone poultry, agricultural or generic traceability matches.

Fisheries quota, TAC and fishing-opportunity instruments are in scope where they regulate fish stocks, catching limits, fishing opportunities, fishing effort, vessels, landings or commercial fisheries management; non-fish tariff quota instruments are out of scope.
seed_query_notes: Prefer fisheries-law anchors and combinations of fish/shellfish/fishery products with import, export, trade, marketing, labelling, processing, aquaculture, farmed fish, quotas, TAC, fishing vessels, live bivalve molluscs, fishmeal, caviar or isinglass.

Do not emit weak standalone terms (roe, fish eggs, fish hatchery, fish pellets, fish bladders, sturgeon products, seafood, seafood trade, seafood marketing, fish traceability, molluscs, crustaceans, quota, quotas, TAC) as discovery queries; use contextual fish/fisheries quota compounds instead.

Use exclusion terms such as ornamental, aquarium, pet, angling, recreational, sport fishing, research, conservation, biodiversity, cosmetics, medical, wound dressing, collagen, poultry hatchery and agricultural traceability to down-rank false positives rather than automatically reject mixed-purpose fisheries sources.
